validity.recommendation: Revise StartYear (2017 -> 2015/2016) and replace placeholder Capacity (1.00 MMcf/d is implausible); re-derive LengthKnown (80 km not cleanly supported); confirm P7766/P7767 are the documented twin trunklines and not a double-count.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED. The Hasbah-to-Wasit gas pipeline is real and independently documented. Oil & Gas Journal (24 Mar 2016) reports Aramco commissioned the offshore Hasbah field, part of the two-field Al Wasit gas project, and that 'Twin 36-in. trunklines will carry production from the fields to the Wasit gas plant.' Offshore-Technology's Al Wasit Gas Program and Hasbah Gas Field Expansion pages independently describe a 36in-diameter export pipeline from the Hasbah tie-in platforms to the Wasit gas plant. These are separate origins, not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED as a dry-gas transmission trunkline (non-associated sour gas from Hasbah to the onshore Wasit processing plant; NGL is extracted downstream at the plant, so the trunkline itself is correctly gas/transmission). FuelSource = Hasbah Gas Field: CONFIRMED. Owner = Aramco 100%: CONFIRMED (wholly Aramco mega-project). Diameter = 36 in: CONFIRMED HIGH by 3 independent sources (OGJ 'Twin 36-in. trunklines'; Offshore-Technology Al Wasit '36in in diameter'; Offshore-Technology Hasbah Expansion '36in-diameter pipeline'). DUPLICATE: P7766 (Pipeline 1) and P7767 (Pipeline 2), both 80 km / 36 in, plausibly correspond to the documented TWIN trunklines, so they are most likely two genuine parallel lines rather than a relabel double-count -- but this should be confirmed; if GEM intends them as the twin pair, that is consistent with sources. SPEC CONCERNS: (1) Capacity 1.00 MMcf/d is almost certainly an erroneous placeholder -- the Al Wasit program processes 2.5 bscfd (2,500 MMcf/d) combined Hasbah+Arabiyah; a single 36-in offshore trunkline carries on the order of 1+ bscf/d, not 1 MMcf/d. Recommend blanking or correcting. (2) StartYear1 = 2017 conflicts with independent sources: Wasit plant came onstream Oct 2015, Hasbah first gas reported Oct 2015/March 2016 (OGJ commissioning 24 Mar 2016; Argaam/Offshore-Energy 'Aramco starts gas production at Hasbah field'). The feeder trunkline was operational by 2015-2016, so 2017 is 1-2 years late. (3) LengthKnown = 80 km is not cleanly corroborated: Offshore-Technology's Hasbah Expansion page gives the Hasbah-Wasit 36-in line as ~36 km carbon-steel + 1.9 km CRA (~38 km); the Al Wasit program page cites a 260 km export pipeline plus a 120 km onshore pipeline; field is ~150 km NE of Jubail. None of these is 80 km, so the GEM length should be re-derived. Diameter/status/owner/fuel/type are solid; length, capacity, and start year are the weak points.

summary: P7766 Hasbah-Wasit 36-in gas trunkline EXISTS and is correctly classified (gas transmission, Aramco, Hasbah field); concern=spec: StartYear 2017 should be 2015/2016, Capacity 1.00 MMcf/d is an implausible placeholder, and 80 km length is not cleanly corroborated; P7766/P7767 are likely the documented twin trunklines (not a duplicate).
